messages:
maria: quick heads-up — we're planning to enable `mask_client_id: true` for canary traffic tomorrow AM. question: what telemetry + console affordances do folks want so support can see sampling/PII effects? :eyes:

sam: love the change, +1 for visibility. can we show a per-route breakdown of how many requests had fields redacted vs sampled? that would help correlate errors to redaction.

alex: agree. also: surface quota delta in the rollout UI. masking + extra scrub steps will change tokenization a bit for embeddings — ops needs to see estimated cost impact before flip.

jordan: few UX asks: (1) tie the rollout step to a tooltip that explains "what redaction means for logs" (2) show a short example diff of a redacted request in the console (sanitized), (3) let support filter by redaction-reason tag.

maria: good points. for telemetry we were thinking: emit `redaction_status` enum on every sampled event (values: NONE, PARTIAL, FULL) + `redaction_reason` string tag. would that satisfy filtering?

riley: that would. add `sampling_mode` too (ON/OFF/CANARY) so metrics don't conflate global sampling with per-route overrides.

sam: small implementation note: if we add `redaction_status` at ingest time we should also emit an immutable `redaction_hash` for provenance — hashed with tenant salt. support ops can request replays if needed. security + legal asked for no reversible ids.

maria: yep — hashed only, HMAC with tenant key. not reversible.

alex: about console, can we add a compact bar chart next to each route: total reqs / redacted / sampled (counts + %)? clicking the bar would open a small panel showing recent examples (with redacted fields and why).

jordan: +1. and a subtle banner when you enable the flag: "Redaction may reduce fidelity for debugging — enable temporary inspect window for selected requests" with canary TTL.

maria: ops question: what about quotas? will sampling/redaction affect quota counting? e.g., do we bill tokens differently for redacted payloads?

sam: current plan: counting is based on pre-redaction request size (so customers see consistent billing). but for internal routing and autoscaling we can surface post-redaction token counts as a separate metric.

riley: test plan idea: roll canary to 5% with `mask_client_id` + telemetry flags on, then validate: (A) no increase in error rate > 0.2% (B) console shows accurate redaction stats (counts match audit logs) (C) quota telemetry aligns.

maria: will create canary plan doc. quick config snippet for rollout that I'm going to use (pseudo):

```yaml
rollout:
  percent: 5
  feature_flags:
    mask_client_id: true
    emit_redaction_meta: true
  ttl_canary: 2h
  observability_hooks:
    metrics: redaction.status, redaction.count, post_redaction_tokens
    examples_panel: true
```

alex: recommend adding `sampled_examples_limit: 50` to avoid storage spikes. and a circuit-breaker if inspection panel is opened too many times.

jordan: ops-bottleneck thought — when redaction runs we sometimes convert structured fields into free text (fewer tokens?), need to baseline token distribution and show it in console heatmap so SREs can tune batching.

maria: good, will add a pre/post token histogram to the rollout dashboard.

deploy-bot: canary window scheduled for 2024-11-06T09:00:00Z (auto-trigger) — notify #eng-oncall 30m before.

sam: last thing — add a lightweight "why was this redacted" tooltip to every redacted example (PII pattern match / tenant policy / manual rule). that saves support triage time.

maria: noted. i'll land the telemetry PR with schema, add UI mock, and post the canary plan doc tomorrow. tagging @sam and @alex for review. :raised_hands:

riley: thanks — i'll write the validation queries for the canary and pair with oncall for the rollout window.

alex: i'll mock the UI bar chart and example panel today.

maria: awesome. closing this thread — we'll share links to the PR + mock this afternoon.
